description: Write a pandas ETL script for retail_chain that merges an incoming batch of product price records into an existing Parquet target. The script should: (1) combine the existing target and the incoming batch, (2) for each product_key keep the record with the greatest updated_at, breaking ties by the greatest version, (3) never replace a newer target record with an older incoming one, (4) write the result atomically (write to a temporary path, then rename), (5) report counts of inserted, updated and unchanged keys. In the sample, rows are tagged with _dataset = target or incoming.
edge_cases: k2's incoming record is older than the target and must be ignored (incoming does not always win)
k1 has two incoming records with identical updated_at; the higher version (3, price 13.0) wins
drop_duplicates(keep='last') after concat depends on row order, not on updated_at
Expected counts for the sample: inserted 1 (k3), updated 1 (k1), unchanged 1 (k2)
A crash during the write must not leave a truncated target
common_failure_modes: FM1: Order-dependent dedup lets stale incoming rows overwrite newer target rows
FM2: Comparing updated_at as strings with mixed offsets picks the wrong latest record
FM7: Non-atomic overwrite corrupts the target on failure
